dimension_grades.evidence: All sections use narrative prose paragraphs rather than bullet points (e.g., 'The team has made really solid progress this week on the Atlas migration. After several productive working sessions…').
There are no bullet points in the draft; information is conveyed in multi-sentence paragraphs.

The payment processor issue is discussed in both 'Blockers and Challenges' and again in 'Next Steps' ('continue debugging the payment processor integration'), and staffing concerns appear in 'Broader Context' as well as implicitly in 'Blockers and Challenges' (slowed velocity).
The 'Broader Context' section about the hiring freeze and burnout concerns could be folded into 'Blockers and Challenges' or removed entirely.
The first line after the greeting is context-setting: 'I hope this message finds you well and that you had a great weekend. I wanted to take a few minutes to walk you through where things stand…'
There is no upfront summary sentence capturing both wins and timeline shifts; these are spread across separate sections deep in the draft.
No summary line exists that signals whether the reader needs to act; escalation is mentioned only deep in the 'Blockers and Challenges' section.
There is no summary line at all, so this dimension cannot be satisfied.
The draft uses alarm language: 'significant setback,' 'serious concern,' 'scrambling,' 'failed during end-to-end testing,' and 'real headache.'
Timeline impact is left vague: 'hope to have a clearer picture of the timeline impact, though it's hard to say exactly when we'll know more.'
No specific date is given for when the resolution path will be clear; the draft only says 'it's hard to say exactly when we'll know more.'
Rather than noting that escalation is not needed, the draft actively recommends escalation: 'I'd recommend we flag both of these to the VP sooner rather than later.'
The draft does not use any internet-style abbreviations or casual shorthand like 'TL;DR'; it maintains a formal tone throughout.

The closing is overly formal and stiff: 'Please don't hesitate to reach out if you'd like to set up time to discuss any of this in greater detail. I'm happy to put together a more comprehensive briefing document or jump on a call at your convenience. Best regards, Sarah.'
The verbose, formal register with pleasantries ('I hope this message finds you well') and lengthy paragraphs is not calibrated for a director who reads on mobile between meetings.
